title: Belize
capsule: Belize, the only English-speaking country in Central America, was a British colony known as British Honduras from 1862 until achieving full independence on 21 September 1981, with Queen Elizabeth II as head of state. Its independence was complicated by a long-standing Guatemalan territorial claim to the entire country, which required a permanent British garrison until 1994. The economy has rested on sugar, citrus, and banana exports alongside growing ecotourism, while the country's Barrier Reef — the largest in the Western Hemisphere — was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996. Guatemala formally recognized Belizean sovereignty in 1991, though a residual border dispute was referred to the International Court of Justice in 2019.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Modern borders are well-defined; the precise western boundary with Guatemala remained disputed but is cartographically documented.
